title: Provisional hold window and soft-credit pilot for enterprise invoices (security-questionnaire gating)
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Problem statement: Enterprise customers completing security questionnaires often request invoice holds, provisional credits, or retroactive adjustments while procurement/legal completes paperwork. Current flow requires manual finance ops and ad-hoc tickets, which increases SLA time-to-resolution, causes invoice disputes, and makes audit trails inconsistent. This ticket scopes a pilot to introduce a configurable provisional-hold window and a soft-credit mechanism for eligible enterprise invoices, plus a gating integration tied to Security Questionnaire status so that holds can be auto-applied or auto-released based on questionnaire resolution.

Objectives: 1) Reduce manual finance interventions for invoice holds by 60% for pilot cohort; 2) Provide clear, auditable metadata on holds/credits for compliance and SOC review; 3) Avoid revenue leakage by limiting provisional credits to defined thresholds and automatic reconciliation rules; 4) Validate UX language for proactive invoice memos so customers understand temporary credits and expected reconciliation.

Scope and proposed behavior: - Add a provisional_hold flag on enterprise invoice objects with: hold_reason, hold_start, hold_end (configurable window), provisional_credit_amount, and linked_security_questionnaire_id (if applicable). - Pilot cohort: enterprise customers in concierge onboarding where security_questionnaire.status in [pending, under_review]. - Soft-credit rules: max provisional credit = min(10% of invoice, $10k) per invoice; finance override allowed via console. - Reconciliation: At hold_end or questionnaire.resolved -> system runs automated reconciliation: if unresolved exceptions exist, escalate to finance queue; otherwise convert provisional_credit to either final credit or reverse it and generate adjustment invoice. - Audit trail and visibility: every state transition emits immutable audit log entry, accessible in Console invoice detail and exported to customer-facing PDF memo.

Acceptance criteria: - Product: Console displays provisional hold with clear expiration and link to security questionnaire and contract owner. - Finance: Automated reconciliation workflow creates a review task if thresholds exceeded or if customer disputes. - Legal/Security: Gating integration demonstrates auto-release when questionnaire.status == approved in sandbox. - Observability: Metrics emitted for pilot: provisional_holds.created, provisional_holds.reconciled_success, provisional_holds.escalated, provisional_credits.total_amount, avg_time_to_settle. Dashboards and alert thresholds documented.

Design and UX notes: - Messaging must avoid implying guaranteed refund — use language: "temporary billing hold / provisional credit pending security review". - Invoice memos: two templates (automated brief + optional expanded) to be used depending on customer preference. - CTA in memo: link to questionnaire status and account manager contact.

Open trade-offs considered: - Size of provisional credit cap: conservative cap reduces revenue risk but may frustrate large customers; decided to start with conservative default with finance override. - Automatic release policy: immediate release on questionnaire approval vs. wait for signed contract; chosen to auto-release on "approved" for pilot but require finance sign-off if > cap. - Reconciliation cadence: real-time vs. batch nightly job. Chose nightly reconciliation to limit load and simplify rollback.

Implementation plan and handlers: - Backend: add ProvisionalHold model + reconciliation lambda scheduled nightly; changes to invoice generation and adjustments API. - Console: provisional hold UI and exportable memo. - Billing pipeline: ensure metering counts continue to increment (no double-billing) and final adjustments recorded. - Integrations: security questionnaire webhook (sandbox), accounting ledger export updated to include provisional hold markers.

Risk and mitigation: - Revenue leakage: cap + finance override + daily reconciliation limits risk. - Customer confusion: conservative messaging + dedicated invoice memo template + CS playbook. - Audit/compliance: immutable logs and exportable CSV for auditors.

Stakeholders and approvals needed: - Finance (billing adjustments) – required. - Legal/Security (questionnaire gating language) – required. - Revenue Ops – consult. - Eng (billing pipeline) – owner: Marcelo Ruiz.

Links / artifacts: - Confluence: https://confluence.internal.redwood/billing/provisional-hold-pilot (draft) - Design mocks: https://drive.internal.redwood/designs/billing/provisional-hold-ui.png - GitHub PR (backend prototype): https://github.com/redwood-inference/billing/pull/2573 - Finance runbook draft: https://docs.internal.redwood/finance/provisional-holds-runbook

2025-02-12 - Legal/Security review: approved messaging wording in principle; requested that "approved" state mapping be explicit and documented. Asked for security_review_required flag to be surfaced on invoice exports.

2025-02-14 - Eng planning: identified dependency on accounting-exports service and on security-questionnaire webhooks. Engineering estimate: 5 points. Blocker: test webhook sandbox access (ticket ENG-9751).
2025-02-16 - Design review: two memo templates reviewed; minor copy edits requested to reduce refund-like language. UX will add inline tooltip explaining "provisional credit" semantics.
